interest: This file provides valuable economic intelligence on East Asian agricultural reconstruction and trade networks in the immediate aftermath of the Chinese Communist victory on the mainland in 1949. It highlights how Taiwan's sugar industry—formerly the linchpin of the Japanese colonial economy—was rapidly reoriented to supply occupied Japan under SCAP, earn foreign exchange through global exports (including Britain, Egypt, and Syria), and grapple with agrarian challenges such as tenant farmer discontent, currency depreciation, and the diversion of fertilizers to rice cultivation. Additionally, the Shanghai and Taipei telegrams capture rare ground-level data on commodity markets, price shifts, and taxation in Communist-occupied Shanghai, alongside notes on Sino-Soviet beet sugar refining in Manchuria.
overview: This file (State Department decimal 894.61351) covers sugar production, trade, and related agricultural commodities in East Asia between October 1948 and November 1949, with a primary focus on occupied Japan's sugar procurement from Taiwan (Formosa) and post-war regional sugar commerce. The records comprise outgoing and incoming diplomatic telegrams exchanged between the Department of State in Washington and overseas posts in Manila, Tokyo, Shanghai, and Taipei. They document Taiwan Sugar Corporation's post-war production recovery, domestic pricing issues, and major export sales to SCAP for Japan, Great Britain, Egypt, Syria, and Southeast Asia, as well as cargo shipping to Yokohama. The file also incorporates economic intelligence on sugar stocks and commodity taxes in Communist-controlled Shanghai, beet sugar mills in Manchuria, and an apparently misfiled military cable regarding Economic Cooperation Administration (ECA) cotton financing under the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund (OJEIRF).

subfiles.about: Lovett instructs the Embassy in Manila to cable latest estimates for 1948-49 Philippine sugar production and 1949 prospective arrivals.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State instructs the U.S. Embassy in Manila to cable the latest estimates for 1948–1949 sugar production and total prospective arrivals in calendar year 1949, including shipments from stocks of the 1948–1949 and 1949–1950 crops. The telegram is charged to the Production and Marketing Administration (PMA) Sugar Branch and designated for distribution to Fred J. Rossiter of the Department of Agriculture.
subfiles.title: Outgoing telegram from Lovett to Manila requesting sugar estimates

subfiles.about: SCAP Tokyo outlines banking channels and letters of credit for ECA cotton purchases under the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo transmits an Army message concerning financial mechanics for Economic Cooperation Administration (ECA) cotton procurement under the Occupied Japan Export-Import Revolving Fund (OJEIRF). Financing terms stipulate equal division of letters of credit between National City Bank, Chase Bank, and Bank of America, advised to the U.S. Treasury through Riggs National Bank. Payment for cotton transported aboard a Norwegian vessel is arranged through the SCAP commercial account.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Tokyo on ECA cotton purchase financing

subfiles.about: Sebald reports that the ship Hai Sui will enter Yokohama from Takao with 9,000 tons of sugar.
subfiles.summary: U.S. Political Adviser William J. Sebald in Tokyo reports pursuant to circular instructions that the vessel Hai Sui is scheduled to enter Yokohama from Takao (Kaohsiung), Taiwan, on September 15, 1949. The ship will discharge 9,000 tons of sugar, with its subsequent port of call unknown.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from Sebald (Tokyo) on sugar shipment from Takao

subfiles.about: Shanghai reports data on Shanghai sugar stocks and prices, Manchurian beet sugar mills, and Taiwan Sugar Company production and exports.
subfiles.from: Walter P. McConaughy (for Peaslee), American Consulate General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Consulate reporting officer Peaslee, via Consul General McConaughy in Shanghai, provides sugar data for an upcoming Department report. The message details domestic stocks in Communist-controlled Shanghai held by the Shanghai Chemical Supply Company and private traders, local pricing in People's Bank notes (PN), and the newly introduced 25 percent ad valorem commodity tax. It further reports on Manchurian beet sugar production in Sungkiang province under joint Sino-Soviet operation, as well as Taiwan Sugar Company's 1948–49 production of 631,000 metric tons, farmer dissatisfaction with low procurement prices, and export sales to SCAP, Britain, Syria, and Egypt.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from McConaughy (Shanghai) on sugar supply, pricing, and Taiwan/Manchuria production

subfiles.about: MacDonald transmits a comprehensive report from Taipei on Taiwan sugar production, export contracts, crop acreage, and fertilizer distribution.
subfiles.from: Donald G. MacDonald, American Consulate, Taipei
subfiles.summary: Consul Donald G. MacDonald transmits detailed statistics on Taiwan's sugar industry, reporting 1948–49 production of 632,000 metric tons and exports totaling 271,000 tons to Japan, Britain, mainland China, Egypt, Burma, Syria, Hong Kong, and Siam. A further 100,000 tons were contracted to Japan and 7,500 tons of crude brown to Spain, while 26,000 tons were lost in a Kaohsiung harbor explosion. For subsequent seasons, production is forecast at 500,000 metric tons due to farmers diverting corporation-supplied fertilizer to rice crops and planting shorter-cycle, lower-yielding cane varieties.
subfiles.title: Incoming telegram from MacDonald (Taipei) on Taiwan sugar production and export estimates
